gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + SP037 400 W kit costs $0.476 per Wh of battery ($913.49 link price ÷ 1,920 Wh) and ships now. That is about 30% less per Wh than the cheapest 400–440 W kit on the cited StormWatts table ($0.68/Wh, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra + 2×220 W). The R2500 V2's 1,000 W solar cap is above the panel's 400 W rating, so by the maker's figures it can take the full 400 W, and a refill takes 4.8 h of full sun at rated output.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited, 2026-11-08) already gives cost per kWh, refill sun-hours and the panel power each station can accept for 11 kits with 400–440 W of panels. It has no ALLPOWERS kit, uses Nov 8 store prices rather than code prices, and its lowest price per Wh in that group is $0.68 (DELTA 3 Ultra) to $0.70 (DELTA 3 Max). Our own page (cited in chat 2) gives price per usable Wh for six BLUETTI/Jackery/EcoFlow kits only. Its 400 W rows are the Elite 200 V2 at $0.78 and the AC180 at $1.30, and it has no ALLPOWERS 400 W kit. No result in either chat has a 400 W kit under $0.68 per Wh.
decides: Price per Wh at the link price makes the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + SP037 the value pick among 400 W kits that ship now: $0.476/Wh for 1,920 Wh and 2,500 W at $913.49. The R3500 + SP037 is the ships-now pick for a bigger battery: $0.501/Wh for 3,168 Wh at $1,586.73. ChatGPT's picks cost more per Wh. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W is $0.687/Wh and a pre-order until Nov 26. The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max + 2×220 W is $0.70/Wh at StormWatts' Nov 8 price. For a shopper who can wait, the BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2×200 W is $0.470/Wh for 3,840 Wh but ships mid-December, and its 400 W of panels needs 9.6 h at rated output to refill it. One caveat: the store's own S2000 Pro + SP037 listing says its polycrystalline panel gives about 55–65% of its rating. At 60%, the R2500 V2 refill grows from 4.8 h to about 8 h.
